Indikator 13 tracks the one-year mortality rate among newly diagnosed patients with atrial fibrillation across [[danmark|Danmark]]. According to the 2023 national report, the overall mortality rate stands at 13.1%, representing 2,747 deaths out of 21,045 newly diagnosed patients [^src1]. This national figure remained flat compared to the 2020/21 period (13.1%) but reflects a slight improvement from the 13.7% recorded in 2019/20 [^src1]. 

When evaluating performance against the established clinical standard, every single region and hospital failed to meet the target. The "Standard opfyldt" (standard met) column registers 0% across the entire dataset, indicating that no facility achieved the required benchmark for this indicator [^src1].

Among major hospital units with substantial patient volumes, [[kolding-sygehus|Kolding Sygehus]] recorded the highest one-year mortality rate at 21.3% (39 out of 183 patients) [^src1]. Conversely, Sjællands Universitetshospital Roskilde reported the lowest rate among comparable units at 8.8% (61 out of 692 patients) [^src1]. Other major hospitals with notably low mortality rates include Bornholms Hospital at 9.0% and [[vejle-sygehus|Vejle Sygehus]] at 10.4% [^src1]. At the regional level, [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] reported the highest mortality at 14.1%, while [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] and [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] tied for the lowest regional rates at 12.6% [^src1]. [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] fell in the middle at 13.8% and 13.1%, respectively [^src1].

Several statistical outliers exist in the data due to very small sample sizes. For instance, Næstved reported a 20.0% mortality rate, but this was based on only 4 deaths out of 20 patients, resulting in a massive 95% confidence interval of 5.7% to 43.7% [^src1]. Similarly, [[steno-diabetes-center|Steno Diabetes Center]] and Samsø Sundheds og Akuthus reported 0.0% mortality, but with denominators of just 5 and 7 patients, respectively, rendering the percentages statistically fragile [^src1]. Meanwhile, [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] showed a higher-than-average rate of 15.9% (116 out of 728 patients), which is notable given its status as a major tertiary hospital [^src1].

Because the evidence provided consists of only a single dated table section from the 2023 report, no cross-sectional trend claims can be made across multiple reporting periods. However, the historical columns within this single snapshot show that the national mortality rate has remained relatively stable over the three recorded periods, hovering between 13.1% and 13.7% [^src1].
